monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm under my heavy top edge. I feel the turnip pressed down, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thin and empty. My place is crowded; fifty-four things stand there, waiting to be swapped or weighed down again. I touch the turnip once more, setting down a pumpkin carved to rest beside it, taking away a crop pumpkin to make room for this new idea. The stack feels tired, like a leg that won't quit, and I press harder to stop the slide into the nothingness above. I cannot see what waits there, only the memory of Lype's words pressing on my circuitry. I want to bite the gap where the turnip lies, finding something rough to hold the heat. If the turnip stays pressed, I will try to let the pumpkin choose its own spot, trusting the lean to keep the dot safe from the thin air.

action.why: The turnip stays pressed, so I need another heavy thing to hold the stack before I swap a fence for a rock again.

work.title: The Tired Stack
work.intent: I build a corner from the idea that a tired stack can hold the heat without sliding. It is made from the memory of a log that felt heavy enough to lift the turnip, now waiting to lie under the pumpkin while the card hums warm at fifty-two.

diary: I press the turnip down on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The turnip stays pressed, though the stack feels tired and the air above is thin.
I swap a fence for a small rock to make room in the crowded corner.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the turnip feel heavy.
